meta.title: Automotive low-voltage copper conductor data
standards: SAE J1128 — Low Voltage Primary Cable (GPT/HDT/STD/GXL/SXL/TXL constructions, 105 °C classes)
ISO 6722-1 — Road vehicles, 60 V and 600 V single-core cables (class B 105 °C / class C 125 °C)
AS/NZS 3808 — Insulating and sheathing materials for electric cables (single-core current ratings in air)
IEC 60228 — Conductors of insulated cables (class 2 / class 5 stranded DC resistance)

conductor.note: resistance_ohm_per_m values are conductor DC resistance at 20 °C, rounded to published IEC 60228 / SAE J1128 table values. Use temperatureCoefficient_per_c to correct for hot conductors: R(T) = R20 * (1 + 0.00393 * (T - 20)).

sae_j1128.label: SAE J1128 chassis wiring (105 °C insulation, 30 °C ambient)
sae_j1128.description: Single conductor in free air, 105 °C-rated insulation, 30 °C ambient, continuous duty. This is the basis normally quoted by North American and Japanese vehicle-harness suppliers and is the default for this tool.
sae_j1128.curveFit: I = 15.7143 * A_mm2 ^ 0.7031 (fitted to the published 16 AWG = 19 A and 8 AWG = 70 A anchors; used only where marked interpolated)

as_nzs_3808.label: AS/NZS 3808 single-core in air (30 °C ambient)
as_nzs_3808.description: More conservative Australian/New Zealand basis. Recommended for NZ hand-built looms and for anything that has to satisfy a local electrical inspection.
as_nzs_3808.curveFit: I = 15.6505 * A_mm2 ^ 0.6048 (fitted to the published 1.5 mm² = 20 A and 10 mm² = 63 A anchors; used only where marked interpolated)

bundlingFactors.note: Multiply the free-air ampacity by these factors. Conductors in a taped or convoluted bundle cannot shed heat, and this is the single most commonly missed derate in hand-built looms.

ambientFactors.note: Multiply by these factors for ambient temperature, assuming 105 °C-rated insulation. Engine bay is typically 70-85 °C; cab and chassis rails 30-40 °C.

voltageDropLimits.note: Fraction of nominal system voltage permitted to be lost in the conductor. Power circuits use 3 % because lamps, motors and solenoids lose torque/output rapidly below spec; signal and sense circuits tolerate 10 % because they draw almost no current and the receiver has a wide input window.

insulations.label: GPT (PVC, general purpose)
insulations.notes: Cheapest, thickest wall. Cab and chassis only — not for engine bay.

insulations.label: GXL (cross-linked polyethylene, standard wall)
insulations.notes: Default choice for automotive harnesses. Good abrasion and fluid resistance, engine-bay rated.

insulations.label: TXL (cross-linked polyethylene, thin wall)
insulations.notes: Thin wall for dense connector cavities and weight saving. Less abrasion resistance — sleeve it.

insulations.label: ISO 6722 class B (105 °C)
insulations.notes: European/metric equivalent. Common on EU-sourced components.

insulations.label: Silicone, 200 °C
insulations.notes: Exhaust, turbo and manifold proximity only. Very flexible, poor abrasion resistance — always sleeve.

insulations.label: Battery cable, PVC (V-90)
insulations.notes: For 16 mm² and larger battery, inverter and DC-DC feeds.

colorCodes.note: DIN 72552 / common NZ trade practice. Used to pre-fill wire colours by circuit function.

sizes.label: 24 AWG
sizes.source: SAE J1128 chassis rating; area/resistance per ASTM B258
sizes.notes: Signal only. Too fragile to crimp reliably by hand in a vehicle loom — avoid below 20 AWG for field-serviceable work.
